acceptance_criteria.criterion: After launching an orchestrator run, the "Waiting for the run to appear in the queue below..." success banner is automatically cleared once the queue table renders with at least one entry.
Error banners in `#orch-preflight-results` are NOT cleared by this logic (only the success banner is affected).
If the queue is empty on refresh, the banner remains visible (it is only cleared on a non-empty render).

summary: Added banner-clearing logic inside `renderQueueTable` in `orchestrator.js`. When the queue renders with at least one entry, `resultsEl.querySelector('.success-banner')` is called and the element removed if found. The logic lives in the non-empty branch only, so an empty queue refresh leaves the banner in place. Error banners (class `error-banner`) are never targeted — only `.success-banner` is removed. The implementation uses the existing `resultsEl` closure variable already in scope within `renderOrchestrator`.

comments.note: The `statusPollTimer` in the Start Run handler (lines ~143–161) polls for a run-status tombstone but never clears the interval reference on view teardown. If the user navigates away while the poll is in flight, `resultsEl` will have been replaced and the callback will silently no-op (because `renderOrchestrator` reinitialises `resultsEl` on each call), but the interval itself continues running. Adding a cleanup registration (similar to `_orchLogPreviewCleanups`) for this timer would prevent the orphaned interval. Low-priority since the effect is benign, but it is mild resource debt.

The `renderQueueTable` function has grown to ~100 lines and mixes HTML string building, DOM injection, event binding, and now state mutation (banner clearing). Consider splitting into smaller helpers (e.g. `_buildQueueHtml`, `_bindQueueEvents`, `_mountLogPreviews`) in a future refactor to improve readability and testability.

comments.note: No dedicated test cases exist for the new banner-clearing behavior. The orchestrator-view.test.ts suite does not cover the scenario: 'Start Run → success banner appears → queue renders with entries → banner cleared'. This means a future regression in this path would not be caught automatically. Consider adding 2–3 tests to orchestrator-view.test.ts: (1) success banner removed when renderQueueTable receives non-empty entries, (2) error banner NOT removed when renderQueueTable receives non-empty entries, (3) banner remains when queue is empty.

The resultsEl closure used in renderQueueTable is captured at renderOrchestrator invocation time. If renderOrchestrator is ever called again (re-render), the old closure's resultsEl reference becomes stale. The current code already handles this correctly because _orchLogPreviewCleanups are drained on re-render and renderQueueTable is only called via refreshQueue (bound in the same render call). No action needed, but worth documenting for maintainers.
